content: Manganese(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula MnSO₄. This compound appears as a colorless, deliquescent solid and is considered a commercially important manganese(II) salt. In 2005, approximately 260 million kilograms of manganese(II) sulfate were produced globally. It serves as a precursor for the production of manganese metal and various manganese-based chemical compounds. Additionally, this salt is used to remediate soils that are deficient in manganese. Manganese(II) sulfate, like many other metal sulfates, can form several hydrated forms, including monohydrate, tetrahydrate, pentahydrate, and heptahydrate. Among these, the monohydrate form is the most commonly encountered. All of these hydrated salts exhibit a faint pink coloration. This pale color is characteristic of high-spin complexes of manganese(II) ions, which have a d⁵ electronic configuration. Applications and Production Manganese ores are typically purified by converting them into manganese(II) sulfate. When aqueous solutions of manganese(II) sulfate are treated with sodium carbonate, manganese carbonate precipitates out. This manganese carbonate can then be calcined to produce manganese oxides (MnOₓ). Additionally, manganese dioxide reacts with sulfur dioxide to yield manganese(II) sulfate. Manganese(II) sulfate is also generated as a by-product in various industrial oxidation processes that utilize manganese dioxide. These processes include the production of hydroquinone and anisaldehyde. Furthermore, treating manganese(II) sulfate with potassium permanganate results in the formation of manganese dioxide, which is a key component in dry-cell batteries.
